Kind.description:
The two kinds of video a household files by resolution, and so the two the quality
model speaks to. Music and books have a different axis and are not resolution
presets, so they are not here.

Named for what is filed, never for the service that files it: whatever curates
television is asked about `Tv`. Read as the media type a service declares, and
accepting the old service-named spellings where a record still holds one.

schema.description: What the operation is asked with.
schema.title: Asked

schema.description:
What a subtitle finder already holds for one \*arr.

Read back so one already pointed at an \*arr is left alone rather than written
again, and so a write can be confirmed by reading it.

**The base path is not part of this**, deliberately: it is normalised on the way
in — `/` is stored as empty — so comparing it reports a difference nobody made.

enabled.description:
Whether the finder is set to use this \*arr at all. Off is the default, and
an address written with this left off is an address nothing reads.

keyed.description:
Whether it holds a key. The key itself is not read back for comparison — a
credential is not something to carry around to decide whether to write one.

schema.title: Watching

401.description: The plugin's key was absent or wrong.
